# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

**By Claude Code** — Correction 2026-11-19. Symbols were uploaded and work: `orca-slicer.exe` and `OrcaSlicer.dll` show debug files found, and every frame is symbolicated. The earlier note was wrong to say the stack shows only handler frames.

**What actually crashes (all 3 events, identical stack):** the app is quitting. During `OrcaSlicer.dll` process-detach, the `std::atexit([] { sentry_close(); })` registered in `start_sentry` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/SentryClient.cpp:175`) runs; `sentry_close` → `sentry_end_session` → our transport `send_envelope` (`SentryClient.cpp:77`) → `Slic3r::Http::perform` (`src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:800`), which starts a `std::thread`. Creating a thread during Windows process shutdown fails, `std::thread` throws `std::system_error` (`std::_Throw_Cpp_error`), nothing catches it, and `terminate()` → `abort()`. The breadcrumbs before it are just what the person did before closing.

**Why now:** our code. The crash is introduced by the Sentry client itself in JusPrin 2.0.1 (commit a14e9d762f, 2026-11-17), so it is new, not merely newly visible. Windows only as far as seen (3 events, Windows 11 26200/26300).

**Fix (suggested):** close Sentry from the app's own shutdown (e.g. `GUI_App` exit, while threads can still start) instead of `atexit` inside the DLL, or have the transport send synchronously when the process is exiting.
EOF

        self.assertTrue(self.printer.current_print.alert_acknowledged_at >

## Your four items

**OBICO-SERVER-B2J (Chargebee renewal):** ignored until it has 10 events in a day.

**OBICO-SERVER-B2F (SSRF probe):** resolved "in next release", with one wrinkle. Sentry anchored it to release 4122 instead of the live 4127. The error itself isn't fixed either: `NotificationSettingSerializer.validate` still reads `data['name']` (`api/serializers.py:331`), so a PATCH without `name` still returns this 500. The live SSRF check blocks the dangerous part. So if someone sends that probe again, the issue reopens, which seems like the alert you'd want. I left it like that.

**JUSPRIN-APP-2 (crash on Windows):** symbol upload worked. Both JusPrin binaries show "debug file found" and every frame has a name. I was wrong earlier to say the stack only shows crash-handler frames. All three crashes have the same stack, and it's the 2.0.1 Sentry code crashing while the app quits:
- `start_sentry` registers `std::atexit([] { sentry_close(); })` inside `OrcaSlicer.dll` (`SentryClient.cpp:175`).
- On Windows, that runs while the DLL unloads at process exit.
- `sentry_close` sends the session through our transport. `Http::perform` (`Http.cpp:800`) then starts a thread, which fails during shutdown and throws an exception nothing catches. The app aborts.

So this crash is new in 2.0.1, not just newly visible. I posted the corrected diagnosis on the issue.

**OBICO-SERVER-B2K (mute after the print ended):** fixed in `backend/api/viewsets.py`. When no print is running, the view mutes nothing and returns the printer's current status with `succeeded: false`. The page ignores the reply, and the status refresh clears the stale alert. I didn't return a 404, because that would make the page's request fail and create a new frontend error. Before the fix, the dev environment gave the production error (500, `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'alert_muted_at'`); after it, 200. The new test passes along with all 77 obico-server API tests.

## Chat-title fix (OBICO-SERVER-B2H and JUSPRIN-APP-1)

- **Server** (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py`): the decode stays strict, as the project's error rules require. It now recovers the exact bytes the 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 apps send by turning the header back into its raw bytes before percent-decoding. A real production header, `ProblÃ%A8me%20d%27importation`, now gets stored as "Problème d'importation". A title that truly isn't UTF-8 still fails and gets reported. All 319 JusPrin v2 tests pass. On the local dev server, the 2.0.1-style header returned 200 and saved the right title.
- **App** (`CloudAccount.cpp`): `percent_encoded` now treats only ASCII letters and digits as safe, not `isalnum`. A new test switches to a French Latin-1 locale: it failed before the fix and passes after. All 611 tests in the agent suite pass. I didn't run the full desktop app.

To run the tests I started the local Postgres and object-store containers, which had stopped. The test account, printer and token I created are deleted.

**Decision needed:** should I commit these fixes? They're in three repos: tsd-enterprise for the gateway, obico-server for the mute fix (I won't touch the submodule pointer), and JusPrin on `jusprin-dev`. I'd commit each one on its own.

**Decision needed:** the JusPrin crash on quitting hits Windows users on 2.0.1. The fix I'd suggest is to call `sentry_close` from the app's own shutdown, while new threads can still start, instead of from `atexit` inside the DLL. Should I make that change in JusPrin now?
Yes, commit

supported".

TSDGZipMiddleware replaces Django's GZipMiddleware. Requests to a tunnel (by
subdomain, by TUNNEL_DOMAIN, or by tunnel port on self-hosted servers) are
gzipped without the random bytes; every other page keeps them.

Chat titles are percent-encoded the same in every language

percent_encoded() kept a byte unescaped when std::isalnum() said so, and
for bytes above 0x7F that depends on the C locale, which wxLocale sets to
the person's language. Under a Latin-1 code page (French, Spanish,
Portuguese Windows) the first byte of "è" (0xC3, "Ã") counts as a letter,
so 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 sent "Problème" as "Probl" + raw 0xC3 + "%A8me". The
gateway could not read that title and failed the whole chat turn (Sentry
OBICO-SERVER-B2H and JUSPRIN-APP-1).

Only ASCII letters and digits stay unescaped now. The new test switches to
a Latin-1 locale when one is installed; it failed before this change.

Kenneth, 2026-11-19: "Yes, fix both".
EOF
